# Macroeconomics Final: 7-Day Schedule
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c1/Supply-and-demand.svg/1200px-Supply-and-demand.svg.png Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/mortarboard.svg
- **Exam Date**: May 17, 2024
- **Study Window**: May 10 – May 16, 2024
- **Daily Commitment**: 2 Hours (120 Minutes)

## Daily Study Breakdown
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg
- **Day 1: GDP & National Income**: 10m Prep review | 80m GDP components (C+I+G+NX) | 30m Active Recall: Teaching GDP vs GNP to a peer.
- **Day 2: Inflation & Unemployment**: 10m Review GDP | 80m CPI calculation & unemployment types | 30m Active Recall: Practice problem set (CPI).
- **Day 3: Aggregate Demand/Supply**: 10m Review Inflation | 80m AD/AS curves & equilibrium shifts | 30m Active Recall: Flashcard creation for shift factors.
- **Day 4: Fiscal Policy**: 10m Review AD/AS | 80m Tax/Spending multipliers & Crowding out | 30m Active Recall: Teaching the Multiplier effect back.
- **Day 5: Monetary Policy**: 10m Review Fiscal | 80m Federal Reserve tools & Money multiplier | 30m Active Recall: Practice problem set (Money mult).
- **Day 6: Comprehensive Review**: 10m Mixed review | 110m Full subject mind-mapping and formula sheet finalization.
- **Day 7: Mock Simulation**: 120m Full-length practice exam under timed conditions with immediate error analysis.

## Active Recall Techniques
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/lightbulb.svg
- **The Feynman Technique**: Explain the 'Crowding Out' effect out loud as if teaching a beginner.
- **Practice Problem Sets**: Complete 10 calculation-based questions for CPI and Multipliers daily.
- **Flashcard Spaced Repetition**: Use digital or physical cards for key formulas like the GDP deflator.
- **Teaching Back**: Recite the 'Three Tools of the Fed' from memory without looking at notes.
- **Shift Scenario Mapping**: Given a scenario (e.g., 'Oil prices rise'), draw the resulting AD/AS shift from scratch.

## Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Khan Academy Econ] https://www.khanacademy.org/economics-finance-domain/macroeconomics
Action: [Button: FRED Data Tools] https://fred.stlouisfed.org/

# Berlin Tech Offboarding Overview
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6c/Aerial_View_of_Berlin_Mitte.jpg/1200px-Aerial_View_of_Berlin_Mitte.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
This document outlines the standard 30-day offboarding procedure for employees in the Berlin office, ensuring compliance with German labor laws and secure asset recovery.

## 30-Day Transition Timeline
- **Day 1**: Formal resignation received; HR confirms notice period and final working day.
- **Day 2**: Department Manager announces transition to the team and begins knowledge transfer planning.
- **Day 15**: IT initiates access audit; Finance provides preliminary payroll calculation.
- **Day 25**: Exit interview conducted; laptop and hardware return scheduled.
- **Day 30**: Final day; all access revoked; hardware collected; final documents issued.

## Departmental Task Checklists
**HR & Legal**
- Verify contract termination notice period (Standard: 3 months, or as per contract).
- Schedule and conduct exit interview to gather feedback.
- Issue the formal Reference Letter (**Arbeitszeugnis**).

**IT & Security**
- Revoke access to **GitHub** and **AWS** environments on the final hour.
- Deactivate **Slack** and company email accounts.
- Recover MacBook, monitors, and security keys.

**Finance & Payroll**
- Calculate final salary including remaining vacation days (**Urlaubsentgelt**).
- Issue the electronic wage tax certificate (**Lohnsteuerbescheinigung**).
- Confirm de-registration from social security and health insurance.

**Department Manager**
- Document all active project statuses and hand over to the successor.
- Organize a team farewell and announce the transition internally.
- Ensure all local files are moved to shared team drives.

## Offboarding Contact Directory
- **HR Department**: Clara Schmidt | hr-berlin@firm.de
- **IT Support**: Hans Weber | support@firm.de
- **Finance/Payroll**: Erika Jung | finance@firm.de
- **Legal**: Klaus Fischer | legal@firm.de

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Download Exit Form] https://portal.firm.de/hr/exit-form
Action: [Button: IT Return Portal] https://portal.firm.de/it/returns

# Order Tax Calculation API
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/Python-logo-notext.svg/1200px-Python-logo-notext.svg.png Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg
This endpoint calculates the applicable sales tax or VAT for a specific order based on the destination and item categories.

## POST /v1/orders/calculate-tax
**Authentication**: Bearer Token required in the Header.

**Request Parameters**
- **order_id** (string): Unique identifier for the order transaction.
- **currency_code** (string): ISO 4217 code (e.g., USD, EUR).
- **items_list** (array): List of objects containing item_id, quantity, and price.

**Request Body Example**
{
  "order_id": "ORD-99281",
  "currency_code": "EUR",
  "items_list": [
    {"item_id": "SKU-01", "quantity": 1, "price": 100.00}
  ]
}

## API Response Standards
- **200 OK**: Calculation successful; returns tax breakdown.
- **400 Bad Request**: Missing required fields or invalid currency code.
- **401 Unauthorized**: Missing or invalid Bearer token.
- **500 Server Error**: Internal tax engine timeout or calculation failure.

**Successful Response Example**
{
  "status": "success",
  "data": {
    "total_tax": 19.00,
    "tax_rate": 0.19,
    "currency": "EUR"
  }
}

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: View API Specs] https://docs.service.com/api/v1/specs
Action: [Button: Developer Portal] https://developer.service.com/home

# User Profile Management
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Slack_icon_2019.svg/1200px-Slack_icon_2019.svg.png Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/phone.svg
Updates the profile information for a specific user. This endpoint is used for modifying public-facing details like bios and avatars.

## PUT /api/v1/users/{user_id}
**Header**: Authorization: Bearer <token>

**Request Body Fields**
- **display_name** (string, optional): The name shown to other users.
- **bio** (string, optional): User biography, maximum 200 characters.
- **avatar_url** (string, optional): Absolute URL to the user's profile image.

## Response Status Codes
- **200 Success**: Profile updated successfully.
- **400 Invalid Input**: Validation failed (e.g., bio exceeds 200 chars).
- **401 Unauthorized**: Bearer token is missing or invalid.
- **404 User Not Found**: The specified user_id does not exist.

## Implementation Example
import requests

url = "https://api.app.com/api/v1/users/12345"
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"}
data = {
    "display_name": "Jane Doe",
    "bio": "Lead Engineer at TechCorp.",
    "avatar_url": "https://images.app.com/jdoe.png"
}

response = requests.put(url, json=data, headers=headers)
print(response.status_code)

### Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Auth Guide] https://docs.app.com/auth-guide

# EcoTrack Product Strategy
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Berlin_Skyline_Night.jpg/1200px-Berlin_Skyline_Night.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
EcoTrack is a mobile solution for Berlin residents to optimize waste disposal and recycling through AI and community engagement.

## Feature Roadmap & User Personas
**Target Personas**
- **The Eco-Conscious Student**: Lives in a WG (shared flat) and wants to ensure the household recycles correctly according to Berlin's BSR guidelines.
- **The Local Cafe Owner**: Needs to manage high volumes of packaging waste and track disposal costs.

**Core Features**
- **AI Waste Scanner**: Instant identification of trash types and correct bin placement.
- **Community Leaderboard**: Gamified recycling challenges between Berlin districts (Kiez).
- **BSR Schedule Sync**: Localized pickup notifications for all waste categories.
- **Business Impact Dashboard**: Analytics for companies to track CO2 reduction.
- **Recycling Hub Map**: Real-time map of local glass, clothing, and electronics drop-offs.

## User Stories & KPIs
**User Stories**
- **As a** resident, **I want** to scan a package **so that** I know if it goes in the Gelbe Tonne or Restmüll.
- **As a** business owner, **I want** to see my monthly recycling rate **so that** I can report on my sustainability goals.
- **As a** competitor, **I want** to see my district's rank **so that** I am motivated to recycle more.

**Success Metrics (First 6 Months)**
- **Active Users**: 50,000 monthly active users in the Berlin area.
- **Scan Accuracy**: 95% AI recognition rate for common German packaging.
- **Engagement**: 20% of users participating in monthly community challenges.

## Technical Architecture
- **Frontend**: Flutter for cross-platform iOS and Android deployment.
- **Backend**: Node.js with TypeScript on AWS (Frankfurt region for GDPR).
- **Database**: PostgreSQL for user data; Pinecone for AI vector embeddings.
- **AI Engine**: TensorFlow Lite for on-device image recognition.

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: View PRD Draft] https://docs.ecotrack.de/prd-v1
Action: [Button: Tech Stack Docs] https://docs.ecotrack.de/tech-stack

response_text:
# User Notification System
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/Node.js_logo.svg/1200px-Node.js_logo.svg.png Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/phone.svg
This system manages multi-channel notifications (Push, Email, SMS) for the Node.js platform using a PostgreSQL backend.

## Architecture & API Specifications
**System Architecture**
- The system utilizes a Producer-Consumer model where the API sends events to a RabbitMQ queue, and a dedicated worker service processes delivery to third-party providers (FCM, SendGrid).

**POST /notifications**
- **Request Body**: { "user_id": "uuid", "type": "push|email", "content": "string", "priority": "high|low" }
- **Response (201)**: { "notification_id": "uuid", "status": "queued" }
- **Response (400)**: Invalid payload or unsupported notification type.

## Database & Security
**Database Schema Changes**
- **Table: notifications**: columns (id: uuid, user_id: uuid, content: text, status: varchar, created_at: timestamp).
- **Table: user_notification_settings**: columns (user_id: uuid, channel: varchar, enabled: boolean).

**GDPR & Privacy**
- All push notification content must be encrypted at rest.
- Users must provide explicit opt-in for marketing notifications via the settings table.
- PII (Personally Identifiable Information) is excluded from log files.

## Deployment Checklist
- Run database migrations on the staging environment.
- Verify environment variables for FCM and SendGrid API keys.
- Perform load testing (Target: 500 notifications/second).
- Conduct security audit on the new internal endpoints.

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Full Tech Specs] https://wiki.internal.com/notifications-spec
Action: [Button: Security Policy] https://wiki.internal.com/security-gdpr

Standardized documentation for the microservice handling user lifecycles and authentication.

## Service Endpoints
**GET /api/v1/users**
- **Description**: Retrieves a paginated list of all registered users.
- **Authentication**: OAuth2 Bearer Token required.
- **Response Codes**: 200 OK, 401 Unauthorized.

**POST /api/v1/users**
- **Description**: Registers a new user account in the system.
- **Request Body**: { "username": "string", "email": "string", "password": "string" }
- **Response Codes**: 201 Created, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized.

**DELETE /api/v1/users/{id}**
- **Description**: Permanently removes a user and their associated data.
- **Authentication**: OAuth2 Bearer Token (Admin only).
- **Response Codes**: 200 OK, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not Found.

## Data Models
**User Object Definition**
- **id**: UUID (Primary Key, unique identifier).
- **username**: String (Required, 3-50 characters).
- **email**: String (Required, valid email format).
- **created_at**: ISO8601 Timestamp (Auto-generated on creation).

### Quick Actions

# Python Microservice Template
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/Python-logo-notext.svg/1200px-Python-logo-notext.svg.png Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg
This template provides a standardized structure for internal Python-based microservices using FastAPI and Docker.

## Architecture & Local Setup
**System Architecture**
- [Mermaid Diagram Placeholder: Service -> PostgreSQL -> Redis]

**Installation Guide**
- Clone the repository to your local machine.
- Ensure Docker Desktop is running.
- Run: `docker-compose up --build` to start the service and database.
- Access the API at `http://localhost:8000/docs`.

## Configuration & API Reference
**Environment Variables**
- **DB_URL**: Connection string for the PostgreSQL database.
- **API_KEY**: Secret key for internal service authentication.
- **LOG_LEVEL**: Logging verbosity (DEBUG, INFO, ERROR).
- **REDIS_HOST**: Hostname for the caching layer.
- **PORT**: Port number for the application server.

**API Reference Table**
- **GET /health**: Method: GET | Desc: Health check | Auth: No
- **POST /data**: Method: POST | Desc: Process batch data | Auth: Yes
- **GET /status**: Method: GET | Desc: Service status | Auth: No

## Troubleshooting FAQ
- **Database Connection Refused**: Ensure the DB container is healthy and `DB_URL` is correct.
- **401 Unauthorized**: Check that the `X-API-KEY` header is present in your request.
- **Container OOM**: Increase the memory limit in `docker-compose.yml` for the app service.

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Github Repo] https://github.com/org/python-service-template
Action: [Button: Internal Wiki] https://wiki.org/engineering

# Bookstore Inventory System
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/Web_Development_Icons.svg/1200px-Web_Development_Icons.svg.png Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg
Version 2.1.0 provides robust management for book stock, author tracking, and inventory search.

## Authentication & Policies
**Bearer Token Usage**
- All requests must include an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.
- Tokens are obtained via the internal identity provider with a 1-hour expiration.

**Rate Limiting**
- **Limit**: 100 requests per minute per authenticated user.
- **Exceeding**: Requests will return a **429 Too Many Requests** error.

## Global Error Codes
- **400 Bad Request**: Invalid query parameters or malformed JSON.
- **401 Unauthorized**: Missing or expired Bearer Token.
- **403 Forbidden**: Insufficient permissions for the requested resource.
- **404 Not Found**: Resource (Book/Author) does not exist.
- **500 Server Error**: Internal system failure or database timeout.

## Search Endpoint Definition
**GET /v2/books/search**
- **Description**: Search for books based on metadata.
- **Query Parameters**: `author` (string), `genre` (string).
- **Sample Response**:
{
  "count": 2,
  "results": [
    {"title": "The Great Gatsby", "isbn": "978-0743273565"},
    {"title": "Tender Is the Night", "isbn": "978-0684801544"}
  ]
}

### Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Get Sandbox Token] https://dev.bookstore.com/sandbox

Welcome to NexusStream GmbH. This 30-day plan ensures a smooth transition into our engineering culture in Berlin.

## Phase 1: Setup & Integration (Week 1)
- [ ] Complete hardware unboxing and MacBook Pro setup.
- [ ] Configure company VPN and internal network access.
- [ ] Submit access requests for **GitHub**, **Jira**, and **Slack**.
- [ ] Complete mandatory **GDPR** and security compliance modules.
- **Success Criteria**: Environment is fully functional and communication channels are active.

## Phase 2: Technical Deep Dive (Weeks 2-3)
- [ ] Attend architecture walkthrough of the **Go/microservices** ecosystem.
- [ ] Conduct 1:1 meetings with the **CTO** and **Lead Product Manager**.
- [ ] Review documentation for our core streaming engine and data pipelines.
- [ ] Set up local development environment using Docker and Kubernetes (minikube).
- **Success Criteria**: Understanding of the system design and team workflows.

## Phase 3: First Contribution (Week 4)
- [ ] Pick up a "Good First Issue" from the Jira backlog.
- [ ] Submit your first Pull Request to a core microservice.
- [ ] Participate in a peer code review session.
- [ ] Draft a small technical improvement proposal for the next sprint.
- **Success Criteria**: Successful code merge and active participation in sprint ceremonies.

Welcome to the team! This guide covers your essential first steps for joining our Berlin-based engineering office.

## HR & Legal Requirements
- **Employment Contract**: Signed copy returned to HR via DocuSign.
- **German Tax ID (Steueridentifikationsnummer)**: Provided for payroll setup.
- **Social Security Number (Sozialversicherungsnummer)**: Required for insurance.
- **Health Insurance Proof**: Confirmation of your public or private provider.

## Hardware & Software Provisioning
- **Hardware**: MacBook Pro (14-inch), 27-inch 4K Monitor, Magic Keyboard & Mouse.
- **Core Software**: Git (cli), Docker Desktop, VS Code (with recommended extensions).
- **Collaboration**: Slack for internal chat, Jira for task management.

## First Week Schedule
- **Day 1**: Hardware unboxing, environment setup, and office tour.
- **Day 2**: 1-on-1 with Mentor; overview of the product roadmap.
- **Day 3**: Deep dive into the codebase and local development workflow.
- **Day 4**: Shadowing a senior developer during a feature implementation.
- **Day 5**: Pick up a 'Good First Issue' and submit your **First Code Review**.

### Quick Actions

# Product Returns Procedure
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d4/Seattle_Skyline_from_Kerry_Park.jpg/1200px-Seattle_Skyline_from_Kerry_Park.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
Standard operating procedure for processing electronics returns at Northwest Tech Gear, Seattle. Policy updated: 2023-11-01.

## Return Eligibility & Inspection
- **Window Verification**: Confirm the purchase date is within the last 30 calendar days.
- **Packaging Check**: Ensure the item is in its original box with all accessories included.
- **Serial Number Match**: Verify that the device serial number matches the receipt and box labels.
- **Physical Condition**: Inspect for water damage, cracked screens, or unauthorized repairs.

## Financial & Logistics Processing
- **Defect Returns**: Process a 100% refund to the original payment method for verified hardware failures.
- **Change of Mind**: Apply a 15% restocking fee; the remaining 85% is refunded to the customer.
- **In-Store Returns**: Process immediately at the service desk and move item to 'Restock' or 'RMA' bin.
- **Mail-in Returns**: Log the tracking number, inspect within 48 hours of arrival, and trigger the digital refund.

## Customer Notification Template
**Subject**: Your Refund from Northwest Tech Gear - Order #[OrderNumber]

Dear [Customer Name],
This is to notify you that we have successfully processed your return for [Product Name]. A refund of [Amount] has been issued to your original payment method. Please allow 3-5 business days for the credit to appear on your statement.

Best regards,
Northwest Tech Gear Support

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Return Portal] https://nwtechgear.com/returns
Action: [Button: Internal Dashboard] https://internal.nwtechgear.com/pos

# Berlin Residential Lease Checklist
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b5/Berlin_Mitte_Skyline.jpg/1200px-Berlin_Mitte_Skyline.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
Essential legal and practical points to review before signing your Berlin rental agreement on 2024-05-15.

## Legal Compliance (Mietrecht)
- **Mietpreisbremse**: Verify if the rent is within 10% of the local rent index (**Mietspiegel**).
- **Security Deposit (Kaution)**: Ensure the total does not exceed 3 months of net cold rent (**Kaltmiete**).
- **Notice Period**: Confirm the standard legal tenant notice period of 3 months is explicitly stated.
- **Cosmetic Repairs**: Check for invalid 'rigid' clauses; you are generally only liable for repairs if actually needed.

## Move-in Inspection (Übergabeprotokoll)
- **Meter Readings**: Record current values for Electricity, Water, and Heating (if applicable).
- **Appliance Status**: Test all kitchen appliances and water faucets for leaks or malfunctions.
- **Wall & Floor Damage**: Document any existing scratches, holes, or stains with clear photographs.
- **Key Count**: Explicitly list the number of apartment, basement, and mailbox keys handed over.

## Important Attachments
- **Energieausweis**: Mandatory energy performance certificate for the building.
- **Wohnungsgeberbestätigung**: Required for your residence registration (**Anmeldung**).
- **House Rules (Hausordnung)**: Detailed rules regarding noise, cleaning, and waste disposal.

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Berlin Rent Index] https://www.berlin.de/mietspiegel/
Action: [Button: Tenant Association] https://www.berliner-mieterverein.de/

# EcoThreads Return Policy
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d4/Seattle_Skyline_from_Kerry_Park.jpg/1200px-Seattle_Skyline_from_Kerry_Park.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
Standard Operating Procedure for EcoThreads boutique, Seattle. Effective Date: 2024-05-20.

## Return Processing Workflow
- **Step 1**: Verify the purchase date is within the 30-day window using the receipt or POS system.
- **Step 2**: Inspect items for condition; they must be unworn, unwashed, and have original tags.
- **Step 3**: For standard returns, process a full refund to the original payment method.
- **Step 4**: For defective items, bypass the 30-day rule and offer an immediate exchange or store credit.
- **Step 5**: Update inventory levels in the system and place returned items in the 'Steam/Restock' bin.

## Internal Training FAQ
- **Can we refund to a different card?** No, refunds must always go to the original payment method for security.
- **What if the tags are missing?** We only accept returns with original tags unless the item is proven defective.
- **How do we handle gift returns?** Gift returns are eligible for store credit only, provided the item is in sellable condition.
- **Are sale items returnable?** Yes, the 30-day window applies to all items unless marked 'Final Sale'.
- **Is there a limit on defective claims?** No, quality is our priority; defective items are handled case-by-case at any time.

## Customer Notification Template
**Subject**: Your Return at EcoThreads has been Processed

Hello [Customer Name],

We've successfully processed your return for Order #[OrderNumber]. A refund of [Amount] has been initiated to your original payment method. Please allow 5-10 business days for the funds to settle in your account.

Thank you for supporting sustainable fashion!

Best,
The EcoThreads Team

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: POS Login] https://pos.ecothreads.com
Action: [Button: Policy Wiki] https://wiki.ecothreads.com/returns

# SmartHome-Nexus API v2.1
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/44/Modern_Living_Room.jpg/1200px-Modern_Living_Room.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
Technical guide for the SmartHome-Nexus API, supporting IoT device management and environmental monitoring.

## Getting Started
**Authentication**: All requests require a `Bearer Token` in the Authorization header.

**Python Example**:
import requests

url = "https://api.smarthome-nexus.io/v2.1/devices"
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"}
response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
print(response.json())

## API Endpoints Overview
- **GET /devices**: Lists all connected IoT devices. Params: `room_id`, `type`.
- **POST /devices/state**: Updates power/brightness. Body: `device_id`, `action`, `value`.
- **GET /climate/history**: Returns 24h temp/humidity logs. Params: `sensor_id`.
- **POST /security/arm**: Arms/disarms system. Body: `mode` (stay/away), `pin`.

## Troubleshooting & Rate Limits
**Error Codes**
- **401**: Unauthorized - Token is invalid or has expired.
- **403**: Forbidden - Permission denied for the specific device.
- **429**: Too Many Requests - Limit of 100 req/min exceeded.
- **503**: Service Unavailable - Local hub communication timeout.

**Rate Limiting Policy**
- Standard users: 100 requests per minute.
- Limits are enforced per API key/token.

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Developer Portal] https://dev.smarthome-nexus.io
Action: [Button: System Status] https://status.smarthome-nexus.io

# Remote Engineering Onboarding
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/Laptop_on_desk_with_coffee.jpg/1200px-Laptop_on_desk_with_coffee.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg
Welcome to the team! This 14-day guide ensures a smooth start as a Junior Software Engineer in our remote-first environment.

## Technical Setup (macOS)
- [ ] **Git Configuration**: Set up global user.name and user.email; configure SSH keys for GitHub.
- [ ] **Docker Installation**: Install Docker Desktop and verify with `docker --version`.
- [ ] **VS Code Extensions**: Install Prettier, ESLint, and the language-specific packs (e.g., Python/Node).
- [ ] **VPN Access**: Connect to the company network using the provided security credentials.

## Week 1 Schedule (EST)
- **Daily 10:00 AM**: Team Stand-up (Zoom/Slack).
- **Wednesday 02:00 PM**: 1:1 Introduction with your assigned Mentor.
- **Friday 03:00 PM**: Weekly Retro and Social Coffee Chat.

## Communication & Task Standards
- **Slack**: Response time within 4 hours during core hours; use #dev-help for blockers.
- **Jira**: Tickets must move to 'In Progress' when started; comments required for any delays.
- **Code Quality**: Every PR requires at least one peer approval and passing CI checks.

## First Task: Definition of Done
- [ ] Code follows the internal style guide and passes linting.
- [ ] Unit tests are written and cover the new logic.
- [ ] Documentation updated in the project README or Wiki.
- [ ] Feature verified in the staging environment.

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Onboarding Wiki] https://wiki.startup.io/onboarding
Action: [Button: Slack Workspace] https://startup-team.slack.com

# London Engineering Onboarding
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/London_Eye_at_Night.jpg/1200px-London_Eye_at_Night.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
Welcome to our London-based remote team! This guide covers your first two weeks and local environment setup.

## Two-Week Integration Checklist
- **Week 1**: Complete HR paperwork, hardware unboxing, and initial team 1:1s.
- **Week 2**: Deep dive into the microservice architecture and pick up your first task.
- [ ] Verify Right to Work documentation with HR.
- [ ] Set up company Slack, Jira, and GitHub accounts.
- [ ] Schedule introductory calls with the Product and Design leads.

## Local Environment Setup
- **System**: macOS with Homebrew installed.
- **Python & Database**: Install **Python 3.11** and **PostgreSQL 15** via Brew.
- **Docker**: Install Docker Desktop for containerized service testing.
- **Dependency Management**: Initialize projects using **Poetry** (`poetry install`).
- **Git Hooks**: Run `pre-commit install` to enable automated linting on commit.

## VS Code Configuration
- **Linting**: Install the **Ruff** extension for fast Python linting and formatting.
- **Type Checking**: Enable **Pyright** for static type analysis.
- **Extensions**: Add 'Docker', 'PostgreSQL', and 'GitLens' for a complete dev experience.

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Setup Script] https://github.com/org/dev-setup
Action: [Button: Engineering Wiki] https://wiki.org/eng-docs

- **Right to Work**: Complete the mandatory digital identity verification for UK employment.

- **Friday 15:00**: Team Social and Weekly Retro.

## First Month Performance Goals
- **Security**: Pass the internal security compliance exam with 100% score.
- **Contribution**: Successfully merge at least two Pull Requests to the core ledger service.
- **Integration**: Complete 1-on-1s with all members of the immediate cross-functional squad.

Welcome to LuminaStream! This 30-day roadmap is designed to integrate you into our remote-first engineering culture.

## Core Cultural Values
- **Transparency**: Open access to all project data and decision-making docs.
- **Async-first**: Prioritizing written communication to respect all time zones.
- **User-centricity**: Every feature starts with a clear user problem.
- **Iterative growth**: Emphasizing small, frequent improvements over monolithic releases.
- **Inclusion**: Building a diverse environment where every voice is heard.

## Onboarding Phases
**Week 1: Technical Setup & Orientation**
- [ ] Install VS Code, Slack, Jira, and GitHub Desktop.
- [ ] Complete the local environment setup script (`bin/setup`).
- [ ] Attend the company-wide remote culture orientation.

**Weeks 2-3: Project Integration**
- [ ] Join your first sprint planning and daily stand-ups.
- [ ] Review the frontend component library and style guide.
- [ ] **Milestone**: Submit your first Pull Request for a verified bug fix.

**Week 4: Performance & Goals**
- [ ] Review initial feedback with your Engineering Manager.
- [ ] Set personal growth KPIs for the next 90 days.
- [ ] **Milestone**: Complete your first feature-related task independently.

### Quick Actions

Welcome to EcoStream Solutions! This 5-day schedule ensures a rapid and effective start in your new role.

## First Week Schedule (PST)
- **Monday**: 09:00 Orientation | 01:00 Hardware & Tool Setup | Goal: Access all systems.
- **Tuesday**: 10:00 Team Intros | 02:00 Product Deep Dive | Goal: Understand the value prop.
- **Wednesday**: 09:30 Campaign Review | 01:30 Creative Assets Walkthrough | Goal: Audit active ads.
- **Thursday**: 10:00 Agency Sync | 03:00 Social Media Strategy | Goal: Meet external partners.
- **Friday**: 11:00 1-on-1 with CMO | 04:00 Weekly Marketing Retro | Goal: Finalize 30-day goals.

## Software Access Requirements
- **HubSpot**: CRM and email marketing automation.
- **Google Analytics 4**: Website performance and conversion tracking.
- **Asana**: Project management and campaign task tracking.
- **Slack**: Internal team communication and alerts.
- **Canva Enterprise**: Brand asset management and creative design.

## Success Metrics (First 30 Days)
- **Audit Completion**: Full review of all Q4 marketing campaigns and spend.
- **Team Integration**: Completed 1-on-1s with all direct reports and key stakeholders.
- **First Initiative**: Launch one minor campaign update or social media series.
- **Reporting**: Deliver the first end-of-month performance report to the CMO.

Standard Operating Procedure for the morning shift at Emerald City Brews, Seattle. Date: 2024-10-25.

## Safety, Security & Aesthetics
- [ ] **Security**: Disarm the alarm system and verify all exterior locks are intact.
- [ ] **Lighting**: Turn on all FOH and BOH lights; check for any burnt-out bulbs.
- [ ] **Ambiance**: Set house temperature to 70°F (21°C) and start the morning playlist.
- [ ] **Menu**: Update the chalkboard with daily specials and ensure prices are correct.

## Equipment & Inventory Prep
- [ ] **Espresso**: Perform a chemical backflush on all group heads.
- [ ] **Grinder**: Dial-in the espresso; target 18g in, 36g out in 27-30 seconds.
- [ ] **Dairy**: Check expiration dates on all milks and oat/soy alternatives.
- [ ] **Pastry**: Arrange the display case with fresh deliveries; ensure labels are visible.

## Supervisor Sign-off

- **Shift Lead**: ____________________
- **Notes**: ________________________

# Japan Export Compliance
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cc/Tokyo_Skytree_and_Skyline_at_Night.jpg/1200px-Tokyo_Skytree_and_Skyline_at_Night.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/airplane.svg
Compliance summary for exporting consumer laptops from Austin, TX to Japan. Manual Version: 2023-10-15.

## Documentation Checklist
- **Commercial Invoice**: Required. Must include itemized USD costs and full seller/buyer details.
- **Packing List**: Required for shipments over 5kg (standard for bulk laptop orders).
- **Certificate of Origin**: Required to leverage US-Japan preferential trade tariffs.

## Classification & Exemptions
- **Correct HS Code**: **8471.30** (Portable automatic data processing machines).
- **Duty-Free Threshold**: Commercial samples are exempt if the total value is below **10,000 JPY**.
- **Regulatory Note**: Ensure all laptops meet Japanese voltage and wireless compliance (VCCI/TELEC) if for resale.

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Export Portal] https://export.gov/japan
Action: [Button: FedEx Japan Guide] https://www.fedex.com/en-us/shipping/international/country-guidelines/japan.html

# Remote Onboarding SOP
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/Laptop_on_desk_with_coffee.jpg/1200px-Laptop_on_desk_with_coffee.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg
Standard 5-day procedure for the remote integration of Senior Software Engineers.

## Equipment & Communication
- **IT Setup**: Ship MacBook Pro, YubiKey, and VPN instructions by Day -3.
- **Security**: Verify MFA enrollment and disk encryption on Day 1.
- **Channels**: Add hire to #engineering, #team-updates, and #social Slack channels.
- **Meetings**: Set up recurring Zoom links for 1-on-1s and sprint ceremonies.

## 5-Day Task Checklist
- **Day 1**: IT Setup & Security. Mentor intro. [IT Support / HR]
- **Day 2**: Communication & Culture. Async-first training. [HR / Manager]
- **Day 3**: Technical Access. GitHub & Jira provisioning. [IT Support / Manager]
- **Day 4**: Project Deep-dive. Architecture walkthrough. [Manager / Mentor]
- **Day 5**: Buddy Integration. First 1-on-1 and social intro. [Mentor / HR]

## Departmental Responsibilities
- **Hiring Manager**: Schedule all 1-on-1s and provide the technical roadmap.
- **HR Coordinator**: Verify legal documents and facilitate the buddy system.
- **IT Support**: Ensure all hardware reaches the employee and access is granted.

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Onboarding Wiki] https://wiki.techcorp.io/onboarding
Action: [Button: Hardware Tracking] https://logistics.techcorp.io/shipments

# Expense Reimbursement Policy
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Credit_Card_Icons.svg/1200px-Credit_Card_Icons.svg.png Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-rupee.svg
Formal policy and procedure for remote-work equipment and recurring expense reimbursement.

## Eligibility & Pre-Approved Items
- **Eligibility**: All full-time, permanent employees working remotely.
- **Ergonomic Chairs**: Up to **$300** (one-time benefit).
- **Monitors**: Up to **$250** (one-time benefit).
- **High-Speed Internet**: Up to **$60/month** (recurring benefit).

## Submission & Documentation
- **Process**: Submit all claims via the **Internal Employee Portal** under 'Expenses'.
- **Receipts**: Clear digital copies (PDF/JPG) showing the date, item, and total cost.
- **Approval**: Attach the manager's approval email for any hardware exceeding $100.

## Reimbursement Timeline
- **Submitted by 1st**: Paid by the **15th** of the same month.
- **Submitted by 15th**: Paid by the **30th** of the same month.
- **Delayed Submissions**: Will be processed in the following payroll cycle.

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Expense Portal] https://portal.company.com/expenses
Action: [Button: HR Wiki] https://wiki.company.com/hr-benefits

Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/Python-logo-notext.svg/1200px-Python-logo-notext.svg.png Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg
Automated data cleaning and sanitization library for Python, optimized for CSV and Pandas DataFrames.

## Core Features
- **Duplicate Removal**: Intelligent row deletion based on specified primary keys.
- **Outlier Detection**: IQR-based identification using the standard 1.5x threshold.
- **Date-Time Parsing**: Automatic conversion of ISO 8601 strings to datetime objects.
- **Null Imputation**: Fills missing values using calculated column means.

## Quick Start Guide
**Installation**:
`pip install datasanitizer-pro`

**Usage Example**:
import pandas as pd
from datasanitizer import Sanitize

df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
clean_df = Sanitize.clean(df, primary_key='id', handle_outliers=True)
print(clean_df.head())

## Documentation & License
- **License**: MIT Open Source License.
- **Compatibility**: Python 3.8+ and Pandas 2.0+.

Standard Operating Procedure for Green Coffee evaluation at our Seattle roastery.

- **Moisture Analysis**: Use the Grainer II tester; ensure green beans fall within the **10-12%** target range.
- **Defect Sorting**: Follow SCAA protocols to identify Primary and Secondary defects for specialty grade.
- **Sample Roasting**: Roast 100g batches for **8-12 minutes** to a light-medium (cupping) profile.
- **Cupping Evaluation**: Perform sensory analysis using the 100-point SCA scoring sheet.

## Supplies Checklist
- [ ] Grainer II Moisture Meter
- [ ] SCAA Defect Reference Cards
- [ ] 100g Sample Roaster (IKAVA/Bullet)
- [ ] Cupping Bowls and Spoons

- **Day 4**: Peer code review session; shadow a senior dev on a bug fix.
- **Day 5**: Final first-week sync and goal setting for the next 30 days.

## Communication Protocols
- **Slack**: Core availability 09:00 - 17:00 CST; use #dev-announcements for updates.
- **Jira**: Tickets must be updated daily with progress notes and time logging.

# EcoSync Home Automation API
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/44/Modern_Living_Room.jpg/1200px-Modern_Living_Room.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
Version 2.1.0 documentation for the EcoSync SDK, enabling seamless control of smart home hardware.

## Getting Started
**Prerequisites**: Node.js v18+ and NPM v9+ must be installed on your development machine.

**Installation**:
`npm install ecosync-sdk`

**Authentication**: All requests require an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. Tokens are generated via the developer portal.

## API Reference
- **GET /v2/devices**: Lists all connected hardware including status and metadata.
- **PATCH /v2/devices/{id}/power**: Toggles the power state of a specific device.

## Common Error Codes
- **401 Unauthorized**: Missing or invalid Bearer token.
- **404 Not Found**: The specified device ID does not exist.
- **500 Server Error**: Internal system failure; please check the status page.

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Developer Portal] https://dev.ecosync.io
Action: [Button: System Status] https://status.ecosync.io

# Berlin Residential Lease Guide
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b5/Berlin_Mitte_Skyline.jpg/1200px-Berlin_Mitte_Skyline.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
Professional documentation checklist for private landlords in Berlin, aligned with 2023 German tenancy laws.

## Legal & Financial Requirements
- **Security Deposit (Kaution)**: Limited to 3 months of net cold rent; must be stored in a separate interest-bearing account.
- **Pet Policy**: Small dogs and cats are generally permitted; larger breeds require explicit prior written consent.
- **Cosmetic Repairs**: Clauses must not be 'rigid'; tenant is only responsible for repairs based on actual wear and tear.

## Mandatory Attachments
- **Energieausweis**: Current Energy Performance Certificate for the property.
- **Übergabeprotokoll**: Detailed move-in protocol signed by both parties.
- **Identity Verification**: Copies of valid government-issued ID for all named tenants.

## Maintenance & Utilities
- **Nebenkosten**: Detailed breakdown of operating costs (Water, Trash, Heating).
- **Maintenance**: Landlord is responsible for major structural repairs; tenant handles minor 'Kleinreparaturen' up to €100.

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Rent Index 2023] https://www.berlin.de/mietspiegel/
Action: [Button: Landlord Association] https://www.haus-und-grund-berlin.de/

# Classic Film Noir Selection
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Double_Indemnity_%281944_poster%29.jpg/800px-Double_Indemnity_%281944_poster%29.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/ticket-perforated.svg
This curated selection for the London community center highlights the definitive shadows and suspense of the noir era. The screening order is designed to build tension, starting with a shorter atmospheric mystery and ending with a high-impact classic.

## Screening Sequence & Schedule
Film Title | Release | Director | Runtime
Laura | 1944 | Otto Preminger | 88 min
The Maltese Falcon | 1941 | John Huston | 100 min
The Big Sleep | 1946 | Howard Hawks | 114 min
Double Indemnity | 1944 | Billy Wilder | 107 min
Sunset Boulevard | 1950 | Billy Wilder | 110 min

Film Plot Summaries
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg
- Laura: A detective falls in love with the woman whose murder he is investigating. A twist reveals she may still be alive.
- The Maltese Falcon: A private eye takes on a case that involves three eccentric criminals. They all hunt for a priceless statuette.
- The Big Sleep: Private investigator Philip Marlowe is hired by a wealthy family. He quickly becomes entangled in a web of murder and blackmail.
- Double Indemnity: An insurance salesman is tricked into a murder scheme by a provocative housewife. They attempt to claim a double indemnity payout.
- Sunset Boulevard: A struggling screenwriter develops a dangerous relationship with a faded silent film star. She dreams of a desperate comeback.

Action: [Button: BFI Noir Guide] https://www.bfi.org.uk/news/where-begin-film-noir

# Seattle Coffee Marketing Strategy
## QR Code Type Comparison
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/be/Seattle_Skyline_at_Night.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
| Criteria | Static QR Codes | Dynamic QR Codes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| URL Editability | Permanent/Fixed | Changeable anytime |
| Scan Metrics | No tracking data | Location, Time, Device |
| Visual Density | High (complex) | Low (clean) |
| Primary Cost | Free / One-time | Monthly Subscription |
| Best Use Case | Permanent posters | Loyalty cards/promos |

## Pre-Print Testing Checklist
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/ticket-perforated.svg
- **Distance Test**: Scan at the maximum intended distance (e.g., across a table).
- **Lighting Test**: Verify scannability in low-light and high-glare environments.
- **Link Validation**: Ensure the destination URL is active and mobile-optimized.
- **App Compatibility**: Test with default camera apps on both iOS and Android.
- **Error Correction**: Ensure the code works even if 15-25% is obscured.

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Compare All Plans] https://www.qr-code-generator.com/pricing/
Action: [Button: Official Guidelines] https://www.seattle.gov/business-license-and-taxes

### Sources
- QR Code Technical Standards: https://www.iso.org/standard/62021.html
- Seattle Small Business Support: https://www.seattle.gov/office-of-economic-development

# The Green Bistro Digital Menu
## QR Code Setup and Specifications
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/02/Portland_and_Mt._Hood.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
| Feature | Static QR Codes | Dynamic QR Codes |

| Analytics | Basic / None | Scans, Time, Location |
| Link Flexibility | Reprint required to update | Remote URL updates supported |
| QR Print Size | 3.5cm x 3.5cm | 2.5cm x 2.5cm |
| Visual Density | Dense with long URLs | Sparse and consistent |

## Error Correction and Print Standards
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Physical Print Size**: For 18-inch scanning, a minimum size of **2.5cm (1 inch)** is recommended.
- **Error Correction Levels**: L (7%), M (15%), Q (25%), H (30%).
- **Recommendation**: Use **Level Q (25%)** for high-traffic dining to handle minor spills or scratches.

## Pre-Print Scannability Checklist
- **Contrast Check**: Ensure dark modules on a light background with 4:1 contrast.
- **Lighting Test**: Test scannability under dim 50-lux restaurant lighting.
- **Quiet Zone**: Maintain a clear border of at least 4 modules around the code.
- **OS Verification**: Confirm scanning works on iOS 15+ and Android 12+ default cameras.
- **URL Longevity**: Verify the menu PDF link is hosted on a stable, high-bandwidth server.

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: View Digital Menu] https://thegreenbistro.com/menu.pdf
Action: [Button: Contact Support] https://thegreenbistro.com/contact

### Sources
- QR Code Size Standards: https://www.qrcode.com/en/howto/generate.html
- Portland Business Resources: https://www.portland.gov/omf/brc

# Le Petit Cafe Digital Operations
## Menu Category URL Mapping
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4b/La_Tour_Eiffel_vue_de_la_Tour_Saint-Jacques.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
| Menu Category | URL Structure |
| :--- | :--- |
| Espresso Bar | https://lepetitcafe-paris.fr/espresso |
| Artisanal Pastries | https://lepetitcafe-paris.fr/pastries |
| Savory Lunch | https://lepetitcafe-paris.fr/lunch |
| Seasonal Specials | https://lepetitcafe-paris.fr/seasonal |
| Customer Feedback | https://lepetitcafe-paris.fr/feedback |

## Dynamic QR Strategy: Seasonal Specials
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg
- Dynamic QR codes are essential for the 'Seasonal Specials' because they allow you to **update the destination URL** without re-printing the QR code stickers every Monday.
- They provide **real-time analytics**, which is critical for tracking the success of weekly promotions.

## Management Dashboard Concept
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg
- **Total Scans**: Global counter for all categories across the entire cafe.
- **Scans per Table**: Heatmap of the 12 tables to identify high-traffic seating areas.
- **Peak Scanning Hours**: Hourly bar chart showing when customers are most active.

## Physical Placement Checklist
- **Eye-Level Alignment**: Place codes on table tents at a 45-degree angle for easy seated scanning.
- **Matte Finishing**: Use non-reflective materials to prevent glare from Parisian boutique lighting.
- **Accessibility**: Ensure codes are placed no higher than 120cm on windows for wheelchair users.
- **Branding Integration**: Frame codes with the cafe logo while maintaining a 4-module quiet zone.
- **Routine Audits**: Staff should scan codes daily at 08:00 AM to verify link integrity.

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Open Dashboard] https://lepetitcafe-paris.fr/admin
Action: [Button: Update Specials] https://lepetitcafe-paris.fr/admin/specials

### Sources
- Paris Small Business Guide: https://www.paris.fr/entreprises
- QR Code Analytics Standards: https://www.qrcode.com/en/about/index.html

## QR Code Type Comparison
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a2/Florence_Duomo_from_Michelangelo_Hill.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg

| Monthly Cost | $0 (Free) | $15 - $50 (Subscription) |
| Tracking | No analytics | Scans, Time, Location |
| Content Updates | Requires re-printing | Remote URL changes |
| Visual Density | Dense (complex) | Sparse (clean) |

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg

- **Glare Prevention**: Use matte-finish stickers to minimize reflection from dining room lights.
- **Window Height**: Mount window codes at 120cm - 150cm height for eye-level accessibility.
- **Contrast Ratio**: Maintain a 4:1 contrast ratio between the code and the table surface.
- **Size Consistency**: Use a minimum of 2.5cm x 2.5cm for tables and 10cm x 10cm for windows.

Action: [Button: View Sample Menu] https://bellanotte.it/menu

## Technical Safety Checklist
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/5e/Binary_code_and_lock_icon.png Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg
| Security Feature | Implementation Strategy | Risk Mitigation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| URL Sanitization | Regex validation and protocol enforcement | Prevents script execution |
| Link Previewing | Fetch page title and favicon before navigation | Identifies phishing sites |
| VCard Parsing | Sanitize fields for LDAP/SQL injection characters | Prevents data corruption |
| WiFi Configs | Validate SSID and encryption types (WPA2/3) | Blocks malicious network setups |
| Permission Flow | Request camera access only during active scanning | Enhances user privacy |

# Louvre Museum Tour Scanner
## Scanning Interface Layout
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4b/La_Tour_Eiffel_vue_de_la_Tour_Saint-Jacques.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Central Viewport**: Real-time camera feed with haptic feedback on scan.
- **Low Light Toggle**: Top-left icon to activate camera flash for dim galleries.
- **Offline Indicator**: Status bar icon (Green = Cloud, Orange = Local DB).
- **Manual Entry**: Bottom-right button for 6-digit object ID input.

## Scanner Logic Flowchart
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg
1. **Capture**: Scan QR code or enter Object ID manually.
2. **Validate**: Check local SQLite database for exhibit metadata.
3. **Sync**: If offline, queue timestamp; if online, fetch latest audio guide.
4. **Display**: Render exhibit info in user-selected language (FR/EN/ZH).

## Accessibility and History
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clock.svg
- **Low Vision Support**: High-contrast UI mode and screen reader compatibility.
- **History Log**: List of last 10 scans with exhibit title and time.

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Open History] https://louvre.fr/app/history
Action: [Button: Change Language] https://louvre.fr/app/settings

# Lyon Bistro Ordering System
## QR Code Suitability Guide
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4b/La_Tour_Eiffel_vue_de_la_Tour_Saint-Jacques.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
| Feature | Static QR Codes | Dynamic QR Codes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Daily Changes | Not recommended | Ideal for daily updates |
| Scan Analytics | No tracking data | Scans per table/time |
| Link Flexibility | Permanent | Changeable anytime |
| Visual Density | Dense (harder to scan) | Sparse (fast scanning) |

## Physical Print Specifications
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/ticket-perforated.svg
- **Optimal Size**: For a distance of 30cm-50cm, use **3cm x 3cm to 5cm x 5cm** dimensions.
- **Placement - Dark Wood**: Use a white border (quiet zone) of 4 modules for contrast.
- **Placement - Reflective Glass**: Apply a matte-finish laminate to prevent light glare.
- **Placement - Brushed Metal**: Use high-contrast black modules on a solid light background.

## Customer Call-to-Action
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- **Template**: "Savor the flavors of Lyon! Scan to explore our fresh daily specials and order directly from your table."

Action: [Button: Contact Support] https://bistro-lyon.fr/support

# London Bean WiFi Setup
## QR Code Technical Structure
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/67/London_Eye_at_Night.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- **Payload Format**: `WIFI:S:London-Bean-Guest;T:WPA;P:Coffee123!;;`
- **WIFI:S**: Defines the Service Set Identifier (SSID).
- **T:WPA**: Specifies the encryption type (WPA/WPA2).
- **P:Coffee123!**: The plaintext network password.

## Security and Functionality
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg
- **Security Risks**: Data sniffing on unencrypted networks, phishing via fake QR overlays, and accidental connection to malicious rogue hotspots.
- **Testing Checklist**: Verify password string, check scan distance (30cm), test on iOS/Android, verify range, and check for glare.

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Download QR Code] https://london-bean.co.uk/wifi-qr
Action: [Button: Contact Support] https://london-bean.co.uk/support

### Sources
- WiFi Security Standards: https://www.wi-fi.org/discover-wi-fi/security
- London Small Business: https://www.london.gov.uk/what-we-do/business-and-economy

# Safe QR Scanning Guide
## Quishing Awareness Checklist
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/5e/Binary_code_and_lock_icon.png Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg
- **What is Quishing?**: QR Phishing is a social engineering attack where malicious QR codes redirect users to fraudulent websites to steal credentials or install malware.
- **5 Red Flags**: Sticker overlays, blurry printing, mismatched branding, suspicious URL previews, and requests for sensitive info immediately after scanning.
- **3 Best Practices**: Verify the domain spelling in the preview, check for a valid SSL certificate (HTTPS), and use a scanner app that displays the full URL before opening.

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Report Suspect QR] https://financial-firm.co.uk/security/report
Action: [Button: Security Training] https://financial-firm.co.uk/training

### Sources
- NCSC QR Security: https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/guidance/qr-codes
- CISA Quishing Alert: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/news/securing-qr-codes

# Austin Cafe QR Implementation
## QR Code Type Comparison
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/be/Seattle_Skyline_at_Night.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
| Feature | Static QR Codes | Dynamic QR Codes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Monthly Cost | $0 (Free) | $15 - $50 (Subscription) |
| Tracking | No analytics | Scans, Time, Location |
| URL flexibility | Permanent link | Remote updates supported |
| Ideal For | WiFi passwords | Menus & promos |

## Quishing Prevention Protocol
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg
- **Physical Audit**: Daily inspection of table stickers for malicious overlays.
- **Branded Links**: Use custom domains (e.g., cafe.link) to build customer trust.
- **Staff Training**: Educate team on identifying suspicious QR behaviors.
- **HTTPS Enforcement**: Ensure all digital menus are hosted on secure servers.
- **Link Previews**: Recommend scanners that show the full URL before opening.

### Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Manage QR Codes] https://austin-cafe.io/admin
Action: [Button: View Security Guide] https://www.cisa.gov/securing-qr-codes

### Sources
- Austin Small Business: https://www.austintexas.gov/smallbusiness
- QR Code Standards: https://www.iso.org/standard/62021.html

# Debt Repayment Strategy Analysis

## Method Comparison and Payoff Estimates
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d3/Debt_Snowball.jpg/1200px-Debt_Snowball.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/ticket-perforated.svg

## Avalanche Method: 6-Month Payment Schedule

Unallocated | 9.2% | 0% | +9.2%

## Alignment Recommendations
